cls: Ergot alkaloid (partial agonist/antagonist at tryptaminergic, dopaminergic, and alpha-adrenergic receptors)
quick: Sublingual: 2 mg at onset, then 2 mg every 30 min as needed; max 6 mg/attack and 10 mg/week
May be taken without regard to food; nausea is common
Contraindicated - oxytocic and may cause fetal harm
Contraindicated - excreted in milk; ergotism, vomiting, diarrhea in infant; may inhibit lactation
Alcohol may worsen migraine; no specific pharmacologic interaction
Peripheral circulation/ischemia, signs of ergotism, frequency of use (rebound)
summary: Ergotamine is an ergot alkaloid used to abort or prevent vascular (migraine and cluster) headaches, usually combined with caffeine to enhance absorption. It acts as a partial agonist/antagonist at serotonergic, dopaminergic, and alpha-adrenergic receptors, producing cranial vasoconstriction and reduced extracranial blood flow. It carries a BOXED WARNING: concomitant use with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated because it can cause serious or life-threatening peripheral ischemia (vasospasm and reduced perfusion of extremities) and cerebral/cardiac ischemia. It is contraindicated in pregnancy, vascular disease, sepsis, and renal/hepatic impairment.
indications: Abortive or preventive treatment of vascular headache, such as migraine, migraine variants, or so-called histaminic (cluster) headache

dosage.d: 2 mg sublingually at first sign of attack, then 2 mg every 30 minutes as needed
dosage.n: Max 6 mg per attack; max 10 mg per week

dosage.d: Ergotamine 1 mg + caffeine 100 mg: 2 tablets at onset, then 1 tablet every 30 minutes as needed
dosage.n: Max 6 tablets per attack; max 10 tablets per week

dosage.d: Ergotamine 2 mg + caffeine 100 mg suppository: insert 1 at onset, may repeat after 1 hour
dosage.t: At onset, repeat once after 1 h
dosage.n: Max 2 suppositories per attack; max 5 per week

admin: Take at the first sign of an attack for best effect
For sublingual tablets, allow the tablet to dissolve under the tongue; do not crush or swallow
Do not exceed the per-attack and weekly maximum doses
Avoid use on more than about 10 days per month to prevent ergotism and rebound headache
moa: Ergotamine is a partial agonist and/or antagonist at tryptaminergic (serotonin 5-HT), dopaminergic, and alpha-adrenergic receptors depending on their site. In migraine it constricts dilated cranial and extracranial arteries through agonism at 5-HT1B/1D and alpha-adrenergic receptors and depresses central vasomotor centers, reducing the pulsatile vasodilation thought to cause vascular headache. At higher doses or with reduced clearance its strong vasoconstrictor action can produce ischemia.

absolute: Concomitant use of potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., protease inhibitors like ritonavir/nelfinavir, macrolide antibiotics like clarithromycin/erythromycin, and azole antifungals like ketoconazole/itraconazole) - BOXED WARNING: risk of serious and/or life-threatening peripheral ischemia
Peripheral vascular disease, coronary artery disease, hypertension (uncontrolled)
Use within 24 hours of triptans (5-HT1 agonists) or other ergot-type/ergot-containing drugs
monitor: Peripheral circulation and signs of ergotism (cold/numb extremities, pain, claudication)
Frequency of use (rebound and medication-overuse headache)

preg: Ergotamine is contraindicated in pregnancy. It has oxytocic effects and may cause fetal harm, including reduced uteroplacental blood flow; it must not be used by pregnant women.
lact: Ergotamine is contraindicated during breastfeeding. It is excreted in breast milk and may cause symptoms of ergotism (vomiting, diarrhea, weak pulse, unstable blood pressure) in the infant; ergot alkaloids may also inhibit lactation.
renal: Ergotamine is contraindicated in renal impairment. Reduced clearance increases the risk of accumulation, vasospasm, and ergotism.
hepatic: Ergotamine is contraindicated in hepatic impairment. The liver is the main route of clearance, and impairment markedly increases the risk of toxicity and serious vasospasm.

major: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (ritonavir, nelfinavir, indinavir, clarithromycin, erythromycin, troleandomycin, ketoconazole, itraconazole) - CONTRAINDICATED; risk of acute ergot toxicity (severe vasospasm, ischemia)
Triptans (5-HT1 agonists) and other ergot/ergot-derivative drugs (e.g., dihydroergotamine, methysergide) - additive vasospasm; separate by at least 24 hours
Beta-blockers (potentiate vasoconstriction, risk of peripheral ischemia)
moderate: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., saquinavir, fluconazole, grapefruit juice, fluoxetine, clotrimazole) - increased ergotamine exposure
interactions.food: May be taken without regard to food; avoid grapefruit juice (CYP3A4 inhibition)
interactions.alcohol: No specific pharmacologic interaction; alcohol can independently trigger migraine

common: Numbness or tingling of fingers and toes
serious: Ergotism (severe peripheral vasoconstriction with cold, pale, painful, or gangrenous extremities)
Retroperitoneal or pleuropulmonary fibrosis with chronic use
emergency: Signs of severe peripheral ischemia (cold, blue, numb, painful limbs)

monitoring: Peripheral pulses and signs of ergotism (cold, numb, painful extremities)
Cardiac and neurologic status for ischemia
Cumulative dose and frequency of use to avoid overdose and rebound headache
Long-term users: fibrotic complications (cardiac valves, retroperitoneum, lungs)
counsel: Take at the very first sign of a migraine; it works less well once the headache is established
Never exceed the per-attack and weekly dose limits, and do not use it daily
Stop and seek urgent care for numb, cold, or painful hands or feet, chest pain, or signs of stroke
Do not use within 24 hours of a triptan or another ergot medicine
Tell your doctor about all medicines - certain antibiotics, antifungals, and HIV/hepatitis C drugs can cause dangerous reactions
Do not use if you are or might be pregnant or are breastfeeding
pk: Variable; absorption is erratic, faster sublingually and when combined with caffeine
Peak plasma concentration about 0.5-3 hours after dosing
Plasma half-life approximately 2 hours, but tissue effects (vasoconstriction) are prolonged
Vasoconstrictor action outlasts plasma levels and may persist for many hours
Store at controlled room temperature; protect from light and heat; suppositories may need cool storage
pearls: BOXED WARNING: co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors can precipitate life-threatening peripheral, cerebral, or cardiac ischemia - always screen interacting drugs
Caffeine is co-formulated to improve ergotamine's erratic oral absorption and add a mild analgesic effect
Largely superseded by triptans, which have a cleaner safety profile; reserve for selected patients
Vasoconstriction outlasts plasma drug levels, so cumulative/weekly dose limits are critical to prevent ergotism
Chronic overuse causes ergotism, medication-overuse headache, and rare fibrotic complications (valvular, retroperitoneal, pulmonary)
missed: Ergotamine is taken only as needed for an acute attack, not on a regular schedule, so there is no missed dose. Take it at the onset of a headache, respecting the per-attack and weekly maximum limits; never take extra doses to make up for ones not used.
overdose: Overdose (acute or chronic) causes ergotism: numbness, tingling, severe vasospasm with cold and painful extremities that can progress to gangrene, plus nausea, vomiting, hypertension or hypotension, confusion, seizures, and cardiac/cerebral/mesenteric ischemia. Management is supportive with discontinuation, warmth to ischemic limbs, and vasodilators (e.g., intravenous sodium nitroprusside, nitroglycerin, or prazosin) and anticoagulation for severe peripheral ischemia; maintain adequate circulation and treat seizures with benzodiazepines.
